ceviri.16: Publishing frequency is the measure showing how many new pieces of content a site publishes in a given period.
ceviri.33: How many months should the content calendar cover?
ceviri.34: A three-month window is a balanced range for most teams. Longer plans age quickly when sector conditions change. At the end of three months we lay the calendar out again and update the next period according to the production speed actually achieved.
ceviri.35: How many pieces a month is enough to publish?
ceviri.36: There's no single right number; what decides it is the pace the team can sustain. On small teams, quality production that stays within capacity progresses more healthily than a pile rushed out. We look at three headings when setting the number: writer capacity, the time image production takes, and the proof-reading load. When those three items are worked out in real days, the figure that emerges is the volume the calendar can carry. Raising the figure later is far easier than setting it high and cutting it back.
ceviri.38: There should be one person responsible. Distributed responsibility means delays aren't attributed to anyone.
ceviri.39: Do the publishing day and time affect rankings?
ceviri.40: The day and time have no direct effect on rankings. What does have an effect is regularity. Choosing a fixed publishing day helps the team build a habit, and makes delays more visible too.
ceviri.41: What should you do after publishing seasonal content?
ceviri.42: Don't delete the page; keep it for the next season. When the season closes, rather than putting the content into the archive we refresh its date, its campaign details and its internal links for the new period. The history that builds up on the same address gives a sounder foundation than opening a new page from scratch every year.
ceviri.43: How do we know when a piece of content needs updating?
ceviri.44: We look at three signs: a drop in the click-through rate in the search results, dead links on the page, and out-of-date screenshots. When one of those signs appears, that heading joins the update queue. To decide, we also look at whether the service page the content links to still describes the same offer.
ceviri.45: Which metric should you look at in the first month?
ceviri.46: In the first month look at indexing, not rankings. Whether the pages you've published are found by the search engine and added to the index is the only meaningful signal readable at this stage. A page that hasn't entered the index has no ranking data to begin with; the problem may lie not in the content but in accessibility.
ceviri.47: Does the strategy break if the calendar changes?
ceviri.48: No. A calendar isn't a fixed contract but a managed plan. Rows moving around is natural; the breakdown starts when the change isn't put on record.

ceviri.62: Why Is the Content Calendar Decisive in an SEO Content Strategy?
ceviri.63: A brand's place in the search results is shaped as much by when it writes as by what it writes. Many SMEs in Türkiye choose the right subjects but leave the publishing pace to chance, and so never see the return on their effort. As an agency we see a clear picture in the field: the team with a calendar overtakes the team without one in time. In this piece we set out how timing is built inside an SEO content strategy, which decisions the calendar brings forward, and why the review rhythm is a measurable heading in its own right. The method for choosing keywords we take up in a separate piece.
ceviri.64: A publishing calendar ties content production to a visible and measurable order.
ceviri.66: Why isn't a content calendar just a list of dates?
ceviri.67: The calendar's first function isn't to give dates; it's to tie every row to a search demand, a target page and a measurement day. A content calendar is the planning document that builds those three ties in advance. When the ties aren't built, production carries on while visibility stands still; the team works hard but the gains don't accumulate.
ceviri.68: The calendar's real function is making the production discipline visible. Everyone on the team follows, from a single screen, which heading comes out in which order over the next six weeks.

ceviri.70: — ETBİS is Türkiye's e-commerce information system — the number of businesses trading online rose from 600,800 to 634,611 in a year; that means the number of brands competing for the same search result has risen too. In that crowd, a brand publishing without a plan becomes ordinary. An SEO content strategy turns the calendar into a management tool at exactly this point. ceviri.73: Which decisions does the calendar lock in advance?
ceviri.74: The first decision the strategy locks is the order of the SEO-led subjects. The second is which service page each piece of content will link to. The third is the publishing day itself. When those three decisions are settled weeks ahead, the team doesn't go looking for a subject at the last minute. An SEO content strategy should be read together with the service page goals. Mature copy goes live instead of rushed copy.
ceviri.75: Why is the preparation time part of the calendar?
ceviri.76: You have to plan a piece's preparation window as well as its publication date. In an SEO content strategy, the research, writing, image and proof-reading stages each ask for real days. If the calendar only has the publication date, the team is permanently behind. We write the preparation start date on every row too. That way a delay stops being a surprise.
ceviri.77: What is the link between publishing frequency and search visibility?
ceviri.78: That link is indirect: publishing a lot doesn't bring visibility by itself. Publishing frequency shows how many new pieces a site publishes in a given period; what decides things is that number settling into a sustainable rhythm. A brand that starts at high volume and then goes quiet for a long stretch loses its accumulation against a low but unbroken pace. Rhythm comes before volume.
ceviri.79: Organic reach works cumulatively. Every piece you publish prepares the ground for the next. The most common mistake we see on small teams is promising more than their capacity at the start. A calendar opened at a high pace turns to silence before long. When we build an SEO content strategy we measure the team's real capacity first.
ceviri.81: — TurkStat is Türkiye's statistical institute — set out how widespread internet use is in households; and because search demand fluctuates with the season, the calendar has to account for that movement.
ceviri.82: Which of the four publishing models suits you?
ceviri.83: The first two models work on most teams. A weekly rhythm aims for one piece a week and makes building a habit easier. In the monthly block model, production is gathered into a single week and publication is spread across four; on the agency side we recommend this model for most SMEs. We only offer the quarterly campaign model to businesses whose demand is entirely tied to a season, because the silence in between breaks the accumulation. The mixed model combines new content and updates in the same month.
ceviri.84: How is the timing hierarchy built in topic prioritisation?
ceviri.85: The criterion that sets the order isn't how interesting a subject is but its commercial proximity and its preparation cost. Topic prioritisation is the ordering decision that sets which heading gets published first and which later. Subjects closest to the service that brings in revenue settle into the first quarter of the calendar; general informative content is left to later months. That order affects how quickly the budget pays back.
ceviri.86: We build the order in a three-step arrangement.
ceviri.87: We place the subjects that directly support the service pages in the first four weeks.
ceviri.88: Introductory content answering sector questions comes into play from the fifth week.
ceviri.89: We publish broad guides only once at least three months of accumulation has built up.
ceviri.90: That hierarchy lets you build long-term authority without missing short-term demand. In an SEO content strategy, the ordering decision comes before the production decision. We put the sales calendar on the same table too; we bring forward the headings that coincide with campaign periods. ceviri.94: In an SEO content strategy, the decision to postpone is worth at least as much as the decision to publish. We don't put comprehensive pieces that will take long to prepare and need images and data into busy periods. So the calendar doesn't stand empty when team capacity drops, we keep a pool of reserve headings. Ready subjects waiting in the pool close most delays quietly.
ceviri.95: How do we write holidays and seasons into the calendar?
ceviri.96: The mirror of the decision to postpone is the decision to bring forward. Seasonal movements change search demand; for New Year, public holidays and school periods we publish the content at least four weeks ahead. It takes time for the search engine to discover the page, and content published on the day of a campaign is usually too late.
ceviri.97: At what rhythm should we review the calendar?
ceviri.98: A monthly check is enough for most SMEs; a quarterly check is the right interval for a change of direction. A review means looking at the performance of what's been published and laying out the next period again. Weekly tracking usually produces early signals and leads to needless intervention. That's why we choose the measurement interval by the team's decision speed.
ceviri.99: The shorter the measurement interval, the more noise. It can take weeks for a piece to find its place in the search results; a decision taken on the seventh day is usually wrong. At the monthly meeting we answer three questions: which piece exceeded expectations, which fell behind, and which subject showed new demand. The answers lay out the next month's rows again. An SEO content strategy stops being a frozen document that way. Reading the performance data alongside the signals on the advertising side helps as well;
ceviri.101: — we prefer to look at the same table with that team.
ceviri.102: How do older pieces find a place in the calendar?
ceviri.103: Updating is a kind of publishing too. Every month we set aside one row of the calendar for refreshing existing content. Content refreshing is usually underrated at the planning table. The data and examples in a piece written a year ago may have aged. Refreshing usually asks for less effort than writing a new piece.

ceviri.106: Start Building Your SEO Content Strategy with a Specialist
ceviri.107: We start the work by measuring capacity: we work out together how many pieces a month your team can produce and which service is the priority. Then we build the target page map, prepare a three-month publishing plan and match every row with the person responsible. Those three steps build the skeleton of the SEO content strategy; the setup usually takes two weeks.
ceviri.108: The picture we see most often in the field is this: there's content, but no order. Dozens of articles sit on the corporate blog and none of them feeds a service page. It's possible to lay an archive like that out again without writing it from scratch. Building your publishing plan on your existing assets protects both the budget and the time. If you'd like to work out your brand's publishing calendar together,
ceviri.110: is all you need to fill in. We don't promise without measuring; we build the plan from where the data points.
ceviri.111: What should you look at in the first three months?
ceviri.112: In the strategy's first quarter, look at production consistency rather than SEO rankings. How many of the planned pieces were published on time, which row slipped, and why? Those questions show whether the calendar is realistic. The traffic curve may not become readable in the first quarter. Early panic is the biggest factor in breaking well-built plans.

ceviri.137: Let's work out the route map that suits your scope together; let's settle the steps and the timing.
ceviri.140: Timing is the invisible lever of content production. Of two brands working with the same budget and the same team, as far as we see in the field, the one with a calendar pulls ahead in time. In a professional SEO content strategy we talk about rhythm first and volume second. You can write to us to review your publishing plan or build one from scratch. The first step will be filling in the rows of the next three months together. Once the calendar is ready, the argument about production gives way to an argument about measurement.
